source: Minchat Shai on Gen 43:26 (the Masorah's four dageshed alefs)
claim_en: va-yaviu ('and they BROUGHT him the gift'): the alef carries a DAGESH — one of the Masorah's FOUR dageshed alefs in Scripture (the partner it names: 'and they brought to us, by the good hand of our God', Ezra 8:18; the file's other stations named at Lev and Job) — and SNAPSHOT writes the dot inside the guttural in-stream: the rarest mark in the corpus so far, pressed where the gift crosses Joseph's threshold.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

claim_en: va-yiqdu VA-YISHTACHU ('and they bowed their heads and prostrated'): the span's ketiv/qere lands on the BOW-WORD — written clipped (no final vav), read whole; SNAPSHOT carries the pair as two tokens, the bare written form beside the pointed read form, so the verse's word-count wears the doubling: nine tokens where the eye reads eight.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 43:2 (the Ramah; the Masorah)
claim_en: SHUVU shivru ('RETURN, buy'): lean at the father's bare demand (43:2; its twin at 44:25 also lean per the Ramah) — and the SAME chapter writes the verb FULL at the release: qumu SHUVU (43:13). The full skeleton stands exactly THREE times in the Torah — the release (43:13), the noun 'his return' (14:17, the collision framed), and the tents-return (Deut 5:30); the Ramah's third full imperative is the prefixed gate-run (Exod 32:27, named): lean toward Egypt empty-handed, full with the brother in hand.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 43:10; Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 43:10
claim_en: ki LULE hitmahmahnu ('for had we not lingered'): the had-not word ends in ALEF here, its ONLY such token in the Torah — everywhere else the word takes a final yod (Laban's field 31:42; the enemy's boast Deut 32:27, both asserted). And the Kitzur reads the same verse's seam: the last letters of ki ata SHAVNU ze ('for by now we could have returned') spell the four-letter Name in order (builder-asserted): the Name goes down with the caravan.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 43:4 (the Masorah)
claim_en: NERDA ('we will go down' / 'let us go down'): exactly TWICE in the Torah — Babel's divine plural ('let us go down and confuse', Gen 11:7) and the brothers' condition (43:4); the Masorah's third is Saul's night-pursuit (1 Sam 14:36, named): a descent that scatters tongues, and a descent that buys bread for one house.
middah: E7 (the concordance pair — the same wording at two seats, the Kitzur's reading at narrative strength)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 43:7 (the Ramah; the Hilleli; the Samuel pair)
claim_en: SHAOL shaal ('the man ASKED and asked'): the infinitive FULL with its vav (the Hilleli and every precise book; the Samuel pair named) — and the full skeleton's Torah census is a triple collision: the asking (43:7), the Edomite king Shaul (36:37-38, two tokens), and SHEOL the grave (Deut 32:22): to ask, a king, and the pit share one spelling — four tokens.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 43:7 (the Hilleli; Minchat Kohen)
claim_en: ha-YADOA neda ('could we KNOW, knowing'): its one Torah token, written FULL with the Hilleli copy, many precise books, and Minchat Kohen's none-other-and-full ruling — against Masorah-notes that divide and an old scroll-tikkun's variant: the stream keeps the vav.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 43:18 (the Hilleli and Yerushalmi; Rashi; the Masorah)
claim_en: va-YIRU ha-anashim ('and the men FEARED'): written with BOTH yods — the Hilleli copy alone clips one; the Yerushalmi, every book, Rashi's own note ('written with two yods, and its Targum is fear'), and the Masorah's all-Torah-full rule stands verified across the stream: all SEVEN Torah tokens of the form carry both yods — Gerar's men (20:8), the bundles (42:35), the house (43:18), the sea twice (Exod 14:10, 14:31), the shining face (Exod 34:30), and Seir (Deut 2:4).
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

claim_en: ha-kesef HA-SHAV ('the silver that was returned'): the CLIPPED participle — copies that write ha-MUSHAV here err by harmonizing the sons' word to the father's (43:12 ha-mushav, in-stream one chapter apart, asserted): the letter keeps the two returned-words distinct across six verses.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 43:15/29/31/33 (the Masorah)
claim_en: The feast's once-words, each its only Torah token: u-MISHNE kesef ('and double silver', 43:15); Elohim YACHNEKHA beni ('God be GRACIOUS to you, my son', 43:29 — checked; the priestly ויחנך ('and be gracious to you'), Num 6:25, wears the verb with a prefix-vav: collision framed — Joseph blesses the mother's son with the priests' verb before the priests exist); va-YITAPAQ ('and he RESTRAINED himself', 43:31 — the pair the Kitzur names: Haman restraining himself, Esther 5:10: both begin in sorrow and end in joy, each for its own house); ve-ha-TZAIR ('and the YOUNGEST', 43:33 — Isaiah's mighty-younger named). Three asserted, one checked.
middah: E7 (the concordance pair — the same wording at two seats, the Kitzur's reading at narrative strength)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 43:34 (the Hilleli; the old print; the Masorah's portion-file)
claim_en: MI-MASOT kulam ('than the portions of them ALL'): written LEAN with the Hilleli, the earliest print, and every precise manuscript — an erring printer filled it against the Masorah's own four-token portion-file (this verse's two stations lean, its two others full; the vain-burdens pair, Lam 2:14, named by the Kitzur): Benjamin's five hands ride a lean word.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai + Chizkuni on Gen 43:8/10/11/15/20/29 (the chapter's file)
claim_en: The chapter's pointing file: ha-ZOT ('this', 43:15) with the zayin DAGESHED (checked); gam ('also', 43:8) gimel dageshed, peamim ('times', 43:10) pe soft, botnim ('pistachios', 43:11) bet in clipped qamatz (Chizkuni), lishbor ('to buy', 43:20) bet in clipped qamatz (Chizkuni), yachnekha (43:29) yod in clipped qamatz with resting chet (Chizkuni) — all asserted; named: shaal accented forward against the custom (43:7 — MS's lengthening-stroke excursus), the crowding-dagesh debate at u-mishne kesef (43:15).
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 43:18 (the Hilleli and Yerushalmi; the printed Masorah corrected)
claim_en: be-AMTACHTENU ('in our BAGS'): the Hilleli clips the yod, the Yerushalmi keeps it — and every one of our books keeps it (the printed Masorah's lean-note is the error MS corrects); the vav lean throughout the bag-word's family: the yod checked in-stream.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

claim_en: AN INK COUNT WITH A LETHAL CONSEQUENCE ATTACHED, AND THE TRADITION'S OWN HEDGE WORD IS EXACTLY RIGHT. The chain explains why Joseph died before his brothers: ALMOST FIVE TIMES Judah said 'your servant my father' in his hearing and he kept silent, and the honor owed a father is measured in those silences. Machine-checked: the phrase stands in exactly FOUR places in the identical bare form - 44:24, 44:27, 44:30 and 44:31 - while the FIFTH seat, 43:28 in this block, carries the same two words with a preposition prefixed to each. Five seats; four identical. The tradition wrote ALMOST five, and the ink says precisely why the hedge is there. A count whose approximation is itself confirmed.
middah: ink (your-servant-my-father at four identical seats and a fifth prefixed — almost five, exactly)

claim_en: A TWENTY-TWO YEAR ABSTINENCE PROVEN FROM ONE WORD AT THE END OF A VERSE. R. Levi holds that through all the years he did not see his brothers Joseph tasted no wine, and they tasted none until they saw him - and the proof is the last word of 43:34: 'they drank and became drunk WITH HIM ‹עִמּוֹ› (im-o).' With him they drank; without him they did not. Machine-checked: the word stands once in the verse, in final position, exactly where the argument places it. A claim about twenty-two years of two parties' conduct hanging on a single suffix, and the suffix is where the tradition says it is.
middah: plain (with-him read exclusively — with him they drank, without him not; R. Levi)

claim_en: THE FIVEFOLD PORTION IS IN THE INK AT THE SEAT THE BANQUET DOSSIER NAMES. The standing reading takes Benjamin's five portions at 43:34 as part of a seating-and-serving theater staged to test the brothers, alongside the etiquette of asking after the living at 43:27 and the grace delivered at 43:29. Machine-checked: the count word stands once in the verse, immediately before the word for portions, exactly as the reading requires. A numeric rider on a credited row, opened rather than credited, per the standing guard on counts.
middah: ink (the count word before the portions checked; the seating theatre beside)

claim_en: A MEASURE-FOR-MEASURE PAIRING WIRED AT A PARTICLE THAT IS ALMOST ABSENT FROM THE TORAH. The chain reads Jacob's 'if so ‹אֵפוֹא› (efo) then do this' at 43:11 against the trembling 'who ‹אֵפוֹא› (efo) was it' of the stolen blessing - the same rare word marking the deception and its repayment. Machine-checked across the whole Torah: the particle stands at exactly FOUR seats, and THREE of them are these two scenes - two in the blessing chapter and one here - the fourth lying outside Genesis entirely. The pairing is not a coincidence the chain manufactured; the word's whole Genesis career is the deception and this verse.
middah: E7 (the then-particle at 43:11 and the blessing chapter; measure for measure, E27, the reading)

claim_en: A SURETYSHIP IS READ THROUGH A PROVERB CLAUSE BY CLAUSE, AND A SIX-ITEM PRACTICAL LIST IS MOUNTED ON IT. Judah's pledge at 43:9 is matched piece by piece to the proverb warning of one who becomes surety for a friend - the surety, the handshake, the snare of one's own mouth - and the deliverance read as going to cleave to the dust of the man's feet. Attached to it is a standing list: flee from three things (accepting deposits, counselling a betrothed girl's refusal, standing surety between two parties) and cleave to three (the levirate release, the nullification of vows, and making peace). A law-shaped list mounted on a narrative pledge; the case-anchored shelf will meet these same items at the exam.

check.note: A narrative pledge matched clause by clause to a proverb, carrying a six-item practical list of things to avoid and to seek.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)

claim_en: PRAYER IS SITED AT THE COMPLETION OF THE ACCOUNTING. 'At the time of FINDING' is opened four ways - the completion of the day, of the judgment, of the soul, and OF THE ACCOUNTING - and the father's prayer at 43:14 is placed exactly at the fourth: when he saw the reckoning was finished and there was nothing further he could do for his sons, he poured out supplications. The model the block's operators need for why the blessing comes at this verse and not earlier: petition begins where calculation ends.

check.note: Prayer located at the point where the practical accounting is exhausted, as one of four readings of a proverb clause.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)

claim_en: ONE VERSE READ AS A FATHER'S PRAYER AND AS A NATIONAL PETITION, WITH BOTH RECORDED. At 43:14 the plain reading has 'the man' as the Egyptian ruler, 'your other brother' as Simeon, 'and Benjamin' as himself, and the bereavement as of two sons. R. Yashya ben Levi reads the same words as exile: 'the man' is the Holy One, 'your other brother' the ten tribes, 'and Benjamin' the two remaining tribes, and the doubled bereavement the two destructions - closing 'I shall not be bereaved again.' Neither reading is subordinated to the other; the verse carries a domestic and a national register at once.

check.note: A single verse read simultaneously as a personal prayer and as a petition about national exile, both preserved.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)

claim_en: THE TRANSLATION DOES NOT TRANSLATE THE TABOO - IT EXPLAINS IT. Where the verse says eating with Hebrews is an ABOMINATION ‹תוֹעֵבָה› ('to'evah') to the Egyptians, Onkelos writes that THE ANIMAL THE EGYPTIANS WORSHIP, THE HEBREWS EAT. The largest expansion in the block: the separate-tables fact gets its cause from the translation rather than from the verse, and the cause named is a cult conflict. The unit's separation operator therefore carries a reason the Hebrew never states.

check.note: A taboo term replaced by an explanation of the taboo, naming a cult conflict the source verse never states.

middah: ink (the received translation's rendering)

claim_en: TWO VAGUE IDIOMS OF DREAD ARE RESOLVED INTO TWO NAMED LEGAL HARMS. The brothers' fear that the steward means 'to ROLL upon us and to FALL upon us' becomes, in the translation, to LORD IT OVER US and to FRAME US - domination and false accusation. Both are precisely what they are about to suffer over the planted goblet, so the buffer converts an inarticulate fear into an accurate legal forecast, and the unit's threat operators can name the two harms rather than gesture at them.

check.note: Two obscure idioms of dread rendered as two specific legal harms that the ensuing narrative delivers.

middah: ink (the received translation's rendering)

claim_en: THE TRANSLATION USES THE TECHNICAL SURETYSHIP TERM, AND THE CHAIN'S WHOLE READING DEPENDS ON THAT REGISTER. Judah's pledge is rendered with the legal word for security ‹מְעָרַבְנָא› ('me'aravna') - I will be SECURITY for him, from my hand you shall seek him - which is exactly the register the proverb reading requires; without it the pledge is only a promise. At a second seat the noon meal is read as the FIRST OR PRINCIPAL MEAL rather than a clock hour, a reading that sits beside, and does not collide with, the chain's Sabbath-preparation reading of the same clause.

check.note: A pledge rendered with a technical suretyship term that the midrashic reading presupposes, plus a meal-hour read as an institution.

middah: ink (the received translation's rendering)

claim_en: A SABBATH IS KEPT BEFORE THE SABBATH IS GIVEN, BY EQUAL-DECREE ON A NARRATIVE VERB. 'Slaughter and PREPARE ‹וְהָכֵן› (ve-hakhen)' at 43:16 is bound by equal-decree to the manna instruction 'they shall PREPARE what they bring in' - preparation being a Sabbath word - so the meal at this verse is held to be a Sabbath meal, kept generations before the commandment. A law-shaped claim raised on a narrative verb, and one of the sharpest cases in the corpus of the tradition reading later legislation backward into a story.

check.note: A Sabbath observance inferred for a pre-Sinai meal by binding a narrative verb to a later legislative verb.

middah: E7 (prepare at 43:16 bound to the manna's prepare — a Sabbath meal before the Sabbath; narrative strength)

claim_en: A CENSUS OF WITHHELD GRACE IS SETTLED AT THIS BLOCK'S VERSE, BY A DIFFERENT SPEAKER. The standing grace-census recorded that eleven brothers received grace in Jacob's word while Benjamin's was withheld - and it named the deferral. Here it is paid: 'God be gracious to you, my son' at 43:29, spoken not by the father but by the brother he does not yet know. Onkelos stops on the same half-verse for its own reason, rendering the blessing as graciousness FROM BEFORE THE LORD. A ledger opened many blocks back, closed here, and by an unexpected hand.

check.note: A deferred item in an enumerated blessing-census discharged at this verse by a different speaker than the one who withheld it.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)

claim_en: THE CONFRONTATION OF THE NEXT BLOCK IS ALREADY UNDER WAY AT THE BANQUET, AND THE ASTONISHMENT IS THE PROOF. 'Behold, the kings convened, they passed together' is read as Judah and Joseph, with 'passed' heard as filled with FURY - each king enraged at the other - while 'they saw and were astonished' is 43:33, the brothers looking at one another at the seating. The tribes are made to stand out of it: kings contend with kings, what is that to us. The chain thereby reads a banquet detail as evidence that the duel had already begun, one block before it is narrated.

check.note: A seating-scene astonishment read as evidence that a confrontation narrated in the next block was already under way.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)

claim_en: TWO STANDING MACHINES FIRE ON THIS BLOCK'S FIRST TEN VERSES, AND ONE OF THEM MEETS ITS OWN OBJECTION HERE. The paved-way table - the eleven matched pairs by which the ancestor's descent prefigures the nation's - counts 43:1's severe famine as a named member. And the rule that a certain conditional particle always marks the merit of the patriarchs meets, at 43:10, its own recorded objection: Judah's 'had we not delayed' is a delay, not a merit. The objection is harmonized rather than suppressed - even the delay and the ascent ran on that merit - and the corpus keeps the objection on the record with the answer.

check.note: A standing typological table counting this verse as a member, and a standing particle rule meeting its recorded objection at another verse of the same block.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)

claim_en: JUDAH'S PLEDGE AS SURETY'S ROOT. Whence that a guarantor becomes obligated — 'I will be surety for him, from my hand you shall require him'; Rav Chisda's objection types the taxonomy against Reuben's unconditional form, and the two brothers' clauses remain the classification. Filed F-131, auto-seated (round 34, the inheritance block).
middah: plain (I-will-be-surety as the guarantor law's root; the taxonomy against Reuben's form; Bava Batra 173b)

claim_en: THE CONDITIONAL BAN BINDS ABSENT RELEASE. Judah's all-my-days clause as excommunication law: a ban on condition requires release — his bones rolled forty years though the condition was met — one verse now powering two machines (surety, round 34; the ban, this round). Filed F-139, auto-seated (round 35, the courts block).
middah: plain (all-my-days as the conditional ban's law — release required; Makkot 11b)

claim_en: THE FITTING-SLAUGHTER ANALOGY. R. Shimon requires slaughter fit for eating, derived from Joseph's slaughter-and-prepare order; R. Meir's counter-canon — slaughter from slaughter, not from slaughtering — recorded beside. Filed F-153, auto-seated (round 37, the table-and-knife block).
middah: I2 (slaughter-and-prepare defining slaughter fit for eating — R. Shimon; R. Meir's slaughter-from-slaughter beside; Chullin 85a)
